topics.topic_name: Fundamentals of Agricultural, Fishery, Ecological and Environmental Sciences

questions.q: Minerals essential in very small dietary amounts—such as Cu, Zn, I, and Se—are known as—
questions.explanation: Trace minerals: Minerals required in very small amounts in the diet, e.g., Cu, Zn, I, Se. Macro-minerals: Required in larger amounts, e.g., Ca, P, K, Na. Ionic minerals: Minerals in ionic form (not a dietary classification). Structural minerals: Minerals contributing to body structure, e.g., Ca in bones.

questions.q: The ozonosphere which absorbs much ultraviolet light from the solar spectrum is a layer within the:
questions.explanation: Stratosphere: Contains the ozone layer that absorbs most ultraviolet (UV) radiation. Troposphere: Lowest layer; weather occurs here. Mesosphere: Middle layer; meteors burn here. Thermosphere: Upper layer; contains ionosphere and auroras.

questions.q: A short, thickened underground stem used for storage is a—
questions.explanation: Corm: Short, thickened underground stem used for storage. Rhizome: Horizontal underground stem that grows laterally. Bulbil: Small bulb-like structure that develops on a plant for vegetative propagation. Tuber: Enlarged, usually irregular underground stem or root storing starch, e.g., potato.

ANOVA: Compares means of three or more groups, not directly the relationship between two continuous variables.

Rainfall generated by the movement of air from high-pressure to low-pressure regions is known as:
questions.explanation: Cyclonic precipitation: Rainfall caused by large-scale air movement from high-pressure to low-pressure. Grid-point rainfall: Computed rainfall value at a grid node. Convective precipitation: Caused by rising warm air due to heating. Arithmetic mean rainfall: Simple average of rainfall measurements.

Volume of water that can be released from storage in a confined aquifer per unit horizontal area per unit decline in head is called
questions.explanation: Storativity (S): Volume of water released per unit area per unit decline in head in a confined aquifer. Specific storage (Ss): Volume of water released per unit volume of aquifer per unit decline in head. Specific yield (Sy): Volume of water that drains from unconfined aquifer per unit volume. Specific retention (Sr): Volume of water retained in soil after gravity drainage.

Which of the following options correctly matches ALL terms with their definitions?
choices: Overland flow – water flowing in the channel; Direct runoff – surface runoff only; Subsurface runoff – deep percolation; Baseflow – water that evaporates from soil
Overland flow – that part of surface runoff that flows over the surface; Direct runoff – surface runoff + interflow; Subsurface runoff – same as interflow; Baseflow – same as groundwater runoff
Overland flow – also called groundwater runoff; Direct runoff – only the rainfall reaching the stream; Subsurface runoff – infiltration capacity of soil; Baseflow – flow overland into the river
Overland flow – flow inside the stream only; Direct runoff – evapotranspiration volume; Subsurface runoff – precipitation excess; Baseflow – water flowing on paved surfaces
questions.explanation: Option C is wrong: Overland flow is surface flow, not groundwater; direct runoff includes multiple flow components, not just rainfall reaching a stream; infiltration capacity is a soil property, not runoff; baseflow comes from groundwater, not overland flow. Option D is wrong: surface runoff occurs before reaching the stream; direct runoff is water entering streams, not evapotranspiration; precipitation excess leads to various flows but is not specifically subsurface runoff; baseflow is groundwater flow, totally unrelated to paved surfaces.

In frequency analysis, most hydraulic processes, more or less, follow this process. This process is governed by chance and time dependent. What type of process is this?
questions.explanation: Stochastic process: A random, time-dependent process often used in hydraulic frequency analysis. Deterministic process: Fully predictable with no randomness. Probabilistic process: Deals with probability but is broader; stochastic is a type of probabilistic process. Hydrolistic process: Not a standard term in hydraulics.

questions.q: A technique used to check the consistency of rainfall records of a station:
questions.explanation: Double mass analysis: Technique to check consistency of rainfall records at a station. Normal ratio method: Estimates rainfall at a station using surrounding stations. Arithmetic mean method: Calculates average rainfall over an area. Thiessen method: Area-weighted average rainfall using polygonal regions.

An artesian well is a
Which well consists of connected pipes driven into unconsolidated formations with shallow water tables?
questions.explanation: Driven well: Connected pipes driven into unconsolidated formations with shallow water tables. Jetted well: Uses high-pressure water to drive casing into soil. Bored/Augered well: Dug or drilled using augers, usually larger diameter. Dug well: Manually excavated, wide and shallow.

questions.q: Which logging method uses sensing devices to determine formation characteristics, groundwater quantity, quality, movement, and borehole structure?
questions.explanation: Geophysical logging: Uses sensors in boreholes to measure formation properties, groundwater quantity, quality, movement, and structure. Temperature logging: Measures subsurface temperature. Resistivity logging: Measures electrical resistivity to infer water content or rock type. Radiation logging: Uses radioactive sources to study formation density or porosity.

questions.q: A type of drainage system where laterals meet the main line at only one side.
questions.explanation: Random/Natural: Suited for small or isolated wet areas; no structured pattern. Herringbone: Used on concave or narrow areas; laterals enter main from both sides at staggered intervals.

questions.q: An irrigation canal has the following data: bottom width = 60 cm, depth of flowing water = 50 cm, side slope = 1:1, channel slope = 0.02, Manning's n = 0.035. Compute the capacity of the channel.
A subsurface drain system wherein laterals join the submain on both sides alternately.
questions.explanation: Herringbone: Subsurface drainage system where laterals join the submain alternately on both sides. Gridiron: Laterals form a rectangular network. Parallel drain system: Laterals run parallel into a single main. Double main system: Two mains collect water from laterals.

questions.explanation: Permanent wilting point: Moisture where plants cannot recover; tension ~15 atm. Available moisture: Water between field capacity and wilting point. Readily available moisture: Upper ~75% of available moisture, easily used by plants.

questions.q: Land Soaking Water Requirement (LSR) depends primarily on—
choices: Initial soil moisture and soil physical properties
questions.explanation: Initial soil moisture and soil physical properties: LSR depends mainly on how much water the soil can absorb and hold. Crop variety and fertilizer: Affect growth but not directly LSR. Solar radiation intensity: Influences evapotranspiration, not LSR. Water pH and salinity: Affect water quality, not absorption requirement.

Which irrigation efficiency refers to the ratio between the water received at the inlet of a block of fields and the amount of water released at the project's headworks?
questions.explanation: Conveyance efficiency: Ratio of water delivered to a block of fields to the amount released at the project headworks. Application efficiency: Water effectively used by crops vs. water applied. Storage efficiency: Water stored vs. water supplied. Distribution efficiency: Uniformity of water application within fields.

Which type of weir has a crest shaped to match the underside of the nappe of a sharp-crested weir and has high discharge efficiency?
questions.explanation: Ogee weir: Crest shaped to match the nappe of a sharp-crested weir, giving high discharge efficiency. Glacis weir: Sloped weir, less efficient. Vertical drop weir: Sudden drop, simpler design. Trapezoidal weir: Rectangular or trapezoidal notch, moderate efficiency.

A soil conservation practice that stores runoff temporarily to reduce erosive energy is:
Which structure is placed along waterways or small streams to slow down flow and encourage sediment deposition?
questions.explanation: Check dam: Small structure across a stream to slow water flow and promote sediment deposition. Farm pond: Stores water for irrigation or livestock. Contour line: Line along equal elevation to prevent soil erosion. Riprap: Rock placement to protect banks from erosion, not primarily for sediment deposition.

questions.q: Landslides and slope failures caused by saturated soils on steep hills refer to—
Stones piled and arranged by hand on steep slopes to slow runoff and prevent erosion are called:
It refers to the ratio of the weight of soil to the weight of water with volume equal to the total soil volume
questions.explanation: Apparent Specific Gravity: Ratio of soil weight to weight of water for the total soil volume (including pores). Real/True Specific Gravity: Ratio of soil solids weight to water weight, excluding pores. Specific Gravity of Soil Solids: Same as true specific gravity; only considers solid particles.

questions.q: The _________ refers to the volume of water stored in a reservoir between the minimum water level and the normal water level.
questions.explanation: Active storage: Volume of water between minimum and normal reservoir levels, available for use. Inactive storage / Dead storage: Water below the minimum level, not usable. Live load: Not related to reservoir storage; term used in structural engineering.

An earth embankment designed with sections of varying permeability to regulate seepage through a dam is called—
A rearing strategy where several species are cultured together in one pond is known as:
questions.explanation: Polyculture: Rearing multiple species together in one pond. Sequential farming: Culturing species one after another in the same pond. Alternate stocking: Introducing different species at different times. Multi-batch stocking: Stocking the same species in multiple batches.

questions.q: Aquaponics is best defined as integration of aquaculture with:
questions.explanation: Hydroponics: Aquaponics integrates aquaculture with soilless plant cultivation (hydroponics). Soil fertilization: Not specific to aquaponics. Wetland engineering: Related to ecosystem management, not aquaponics. Mangrove planting: Not related to aquaponics.

The principal type of pond used in aquaculture, suitable across many topographies, is the:
Which structure allows selective release of surface or bottom water layers?
questions.explanation: Monk sluice: Structure that allows selective withdrawal of surface or bottom water layers. Pump gate: Lifts water mechanically, not layer-selective. Overflow spillway: Releases excess water automatically at a set level. Cylinder valve: Controls flow but not specifically for selective layer release.

questions.q: Which aeration system is best for deep ponds requiring oxygen transfer at depth?
questions.explanation: Diffused or bubble aeration: Best for deep ponds, as it transfers oxygen throughout the water column. Paddle wheel: Surface aeration, limited to top layers. Aspirating aerator: Mixes air with water at the surface. Vertical pump aerator: Circulates water, limited depth penetration.
